fullPassage: Every time you conceptualize, categorize, and put a name on something that is not physical but rather consists of pure ideas, you should be aware of a simple fact. Your way of naming, categorizing, and conceptualizing is not the only possible way. Nor is it necessarily the best way. It is vital to recognize that other people from different backgrounds may organize the world and think about it differently. Their approach may be just as valid as yours. Indeed, depending on the context, it may be even more valid. It is easy to imagine that the way we think about the world is the only reasonable way. As long as all the people we interact with share the same concepts and models, it all seems to make sense. But when we interact with people from different cultures or different fields, our habitual thinking may be visible only as one of the many possible ways to carve the world up.
